title: Start May with a Priority Filter
teaser: A new month is a useful moment to separate what truly matters from what merely wants attention.
full_text: Divide May's work into three groups: must happen, valuable if possible, and safe to postpone. Build the calendar around the first group before filling the remaining space.

title: Estimate the Cost of Reversing One Decision
teaser: Not every wrong decision is equally expensive to undo.
full_text: Choose one decision you need to make today and estimate the time, money, or relationship cost of reversing it later. Give harder-to-reverse choices more verification before committing.

title: Name the Cause of One Delay
teaser: Waiting is not always a natural part of the process; sometimes it hides an unnamed decision.
full_text: Pick one delayed item and describe the real reason in a single sentence. Is information missing, approval pending, a queue involved, or is a decision waiting because nobody clearly owns it?

title: Make One File Name Searchable
teaser: Knowing where a file lives is less useful if you cannot identify it later.
full_text: Rename one important file so its date, subject, and version are understandable without opening it. Prefer a pattern that future search can find over vague names like final-final-latest.

title: Choose One Measure for This Week's Main Goal
teaser: Too many indicators can make the most important progress harder to see.
full_text: Choose one significant goal for the week and define the primary measure that tells you whether it is moving. Keep secondary indicators if useful, but make the decision metric explicit.

title: Divide One Purchase by Expected Use
teaser: Total price can hide the difference between something used constantly and something used twice.
full_text: For one expense you are considering, estimate the likely number of uses and calculate the rough cost per use. Do not let that number make the whole decision, but use it to expose usage assumptions.

title: Find the Most Fragile Step in One Process
teaser: A process is often only as reliable as the step most likely to stop everything else.
full_text: Review one recurring workflow and identify the step whose failure would block the entire result. Decide whether it needs a backup person, alternate file, retry path, or clearer recovery rule.

title: Replace One Assumption with a Question
teaser: Guessing another person's intent can create more confusion than asking once.
full_text: In one important conversation today, confirm an assumption with a short question. Be especially careful with dates, priorities, ownership, and expectations that may sound obvious but were never stated.

title: Keep Date and Version Together
teaser: Old and current information become risky when there is no visible way to tell them apart.
full_text: For one important document or dataset, make the update date and version easy to see in the same place. Reduce the chance that an older copy gets reused by mistake.

title: Define What Done Means Before You Start
teaser: A task can keep expanding when completion has never been defined.
full_text: Before starting one meaningful piece of work, write what must be delivered, approved, recorded, or verified before it counts as complete. Use that definition to prevent unnecessary continuation.

title: Check the Recovery Path for One Account
teaser: A strong password is not enough if the recovery channel no longer belongs to you.
full_text: Review the recovery email, phone number, and backup authentication methods for one important account. Replace outdated or inaccessible recovery options before you actually need them.

title: Isolate the Biggest Unknown in One Estimate
teaser: Knowing the largest uncertainty can be more useful than making a detailed estimate look precise.
full_text: For one time or cost plan, write the single unknown most likely to change the result. Gathering information about that uncertainty early may improve the entire plan more than refining minor details.

title: Give One Decision a Review Date
teaser: Some decisions cannot be judged until enough time has passed to observe the result.
full_text: For one meaningful choice you make today, set a date to review it. Record what evidence or outcome you will use so the later review is based on more than memory.

title: Test One Retention Rule against Real Files
teaser: A retention policy that looks tidy on paper may create unnecessary exceptions in practice.
full_text: Apply one archive rule to a real set of files. If the rule creates too many edge cases, simplify it rather than deleting important material simply to preserve neatness.

title: Measure Capacity at Midmonth, Not Busyness
teaser: Feeling busy and having usable capacity are not the same thing.
full_text: List the mandatory work remaining in May beside the time you realistically have left. Before accepting anything new, check whether there is actual capacity rather than relying on optimism.

title: Remove One Field Nobody Uses
teaser: A form does not become better just because it asks for more information.
full_text: Review one field in a form or template that people regularly leave blank or fill without thought. If the information never influences a decision or action, consider removing it.

title: Put an Expiry on Temporary Access
teaser: Access granted for a short need should not quietly become permanent.
full_text: If you have given temporary access to a file, folder, or account, define when it should end. Add a reminder or record so the permission is reviewed rather than forgotten.

title: Read One Percentage beside the Raw Numbers
teaser: A percentage can sound dramatic while hiding a very small base.
full_text: For one percentage increase or decrease you see today, write down the starting and ending values too. Use both views before deciding whether the change is actually significant.

title: Look for Half-Closed Loops in This Week's Work
teaser: Some tasks appear finished even though delivery, approval, or recording is still open.
full_text: Review the items you considered complete this week. Close any unsent file, pending approval, undocumented decision, or unfinished follow-up before carrying the loop into another week.

title: Check Subscription Value against Real Use
teaser: A service can keep renewing long after the way you use it has changed.
full_text: For one upcoming subscription or membership, review actual usage over the last few months. Include frequency and concrete benefit in the renewal decision instead of focusing only on price.

title: Keep One Experiment Focused on One Main Variable
teaser: Changing several things at once makes it harder to understand what caused the result.
full_text: If you run a small experiment today, change one main variable when possible and keep the surrounding conditions stable. Make the observed difference easier to interpret.

title: Transfer Risks with the Handoff
teaser: A handoff is incomplete when the next owner learns what was done but not what can still go wrong.
full_text: When transferring one piece of work, include known risks, sensitive dates, and likely failure points along with the current status. Make uncertainty visible rather than forcing the next person to rediscover it.

title: Count the Decisions from One Meeting
teaser: A long meeting can produce surprisingly little movement.
full_text: Review one recent meeting and count the clear decisions, named owners, and dates that came out of it. If discussion was high and output low, narrow the purpose of the next meeting.

title: Check the Historical Context of One Fact
teaser: Information can be accurate for its original period and still be wrong for today's decision.
full_text: Before relying on one technical, pricing, regulatory, or process fact today, check when it was published or updated. Avoid carrying an old context into a current decision unnoticed.

title: Give One Repeating Task a Single Entry Point
teaser: Requests scattered across messages, notes, and email are easy to duplicate or lose.
full_text: For one recurring workflow, consolidate incoming requests into one queue or record when possible. Reduce the chance that the same work is done twice or forgotten between channels.

title: Standardize the Most Useful Check from This Week
teaser: A good quality check should not depend entirely on one person's memory.
full_text: Choose one check that caught an error or improved quality this week. See whether it can become a short checklist item, validation rule, or automated test for the next cycle.

title: Write the Stop Condition before You Commit
teaser: Knowing when to stop can prevent a weak plan from consuming more resources than it deserves.
full_text: Before starting or extending one plan today, define the condition that would make you pause, stop, or change direction. Make the exit rule as visible as the success criterion.

title: Open One Backup from a Different Environment
teaser: A backup that works only on the original device may not be much of a recovery plan.
full_text: Take one important backup and verify it from a safe alternate environment when practical. Confirm that the data is readable and usable, not merely that a file exists.

title: Clarify One Open Financial Item before Month-End
teaser: Unclear receivables, payments, and expenses become harder to reconstruct as time passes.
full_text: Choose one unresolved financial item and confirm the amount, date, party, and current status. Avoid carrying an ambiguous money record into the next month if it can be clarified now.

title: Close One Long Message Thread with a Current Summary
teaser: The latest state can disappear inside a long conversation even when every message is technically preserved.
full_text: For one important thread, send a short summary of the current status, the decision made, and the next action. Reduce the chance that different participants leave with different versions of the outcome.

title: Close May with Reusable Lessons
teaser: Monthly review is more useful when it preserves methods, not only outcomes.
full_text: Write down three approaches from May that worked well and two mistakes you do not want to repeat. Add one concrete rule from those lessons to the way you plan June.
